completeness_rule: TEDS admissions in every year of the window and total admissions never change by more than 50% year to year (ratio within [0.5, 1.5])
scope: TEDS-A now runs through 2024, so 2023 -> 2024 overlaps part of the decline in overdose deaths (late 2022 onward); earlier years describe treatment admissions before that decline.
coding_shift_rule: first-time share changes by more than 25% points year to year

rules.T1: Heroin's share of primary-opioid admissions fell and 'other opiates & synthetics' rose 2019 -> end year: 'holds' if both share changes have 95% CIs excluding 0 in the main specification AND in the through-2023 specification AND both log-odds trends excluding 2020 have CIs excluding 0; 'partial' if the main specification meets this but a sensitivity does not; 'fails' otherwise.
rules.T2: First-time primary-opioid admissions per 100k aged 18-24 fell 2019 -> end year: 'holds' if the log change CI excludes 0 (negative) for both bounds (missing NOPRIOR as not first-time / first-time) in the main specification, the through-2023 specification and the coding-shift-excluded sensitivity; 'partial' if the main specification meets this but a sensitivity does not; 'fails' if the main CI includes 0.
rules.T3: From 2019, opioid deaths rose relative to primary-opioid admissions (d > 0): 'holds' if d's CI excludes 0 (positive) for start 2019 in the main and the through-2023 specifications; 'partial' if only one; 'fails' if neither.
rules.T4: 2023 -> 2024 (first overlap with the death decline), primary-opioid admissions vs opioid deaths: 'not distinguishable' if d's CI includes 0; otherwise 'holds' for the observed direction (d > 0: deaths rose relative to admissions; d < 0: deaths fell relative to admissions).

source: TEDS-A (SAMHSA): combined 2006-2023 PUF (2015-2023) + 2024 single-year PUF; CDC VSRR state file (xkb8-kh2a) opioid deaths 'Opioids (T40.0-T40.4,T40.6)', Dec 12-month-ending; Census state population (intercensal 2015-2019, Vintage 2025 2020-2024)
method:
Phase 4b: TEDS-A treatment admissions as an independent, AREA-LEVEL signal on opioid addiction.

    python -m src.step_t            # harmonization check, panels, (a)-(d), coverage sims, ledger rows T1-T4

Admissions are not prevalence: they count treatment episodes (not people) at publicly funded facilities,
depend on funding, capacity and referral practice, and miss office-based buprenorphine. Never joined to
NSDUH. TEDS-A now runs through 2024 (combined 2006-2023 file + 2024 single-year file, identical codes),
so 2023 -> 2024 overlaps part of the decline in overdose deaths (which began in late 2022).
